answer.rationale: Competitor price cut has directly triggered churn conversations in price-sensitive SMB segment. memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective for SMB acquisition and revenue with strong lift. memory_57 shows referral incentives work in established customers without retention harm, but current threat is churn of existing accounts, not acquisition. memory_86 and memory_91 address activation and onboarding—valuable for new cohorts but do not directly arrest current churn wave. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) misaligned with SMB-targeted competitor move. A small_guarded_test of promotional pricing on at-risk SMB cohort directly addresses today's competitive threat while preserving ability to layer activation messaging (memory_91) and onboarding simplification (memory_86) for new customers. Risk: promotional pricing can erode long-term unit economics and may create expectation of discounting; this is flagged and argues for narrow, time-bound test rather than broad rollout. Uncertainty preserved: test will reveal whether price-led retention works in this competitive context or merely shifts churn timing.
